A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original approximation-error and runtime experiments using GPT2-large and Llama 3.1 8B on WikiText-103 test text.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A, F, and G report original experiments across four models, including approximation error, runtime, surprisal, baseline comparisons, and pruning sensitivity.

M1.justification: The core covering enumeration, bucket pruning, trie bundling, and conditional generation procedures remain. Appendix G adds optional probability-threshold pruning that skips low-probability bundle extensions. Appendix D also corrects the unbundle end-of-token lookup to use the currently visited prefix.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate next-symbol language modeling on WikiText-103 test text and retain the illustrative GPT2 prompts. Surprisal adds a measurement of the existing task, without introducing another dataset, domain, or downstream task.

E2.justification: v1's aggregate experiments compare beam configurations against a K=128 reference. v2 adds a canonical-tokenization surprisal baseline and an implemented character-level token-healing comparator across four models (Appendix A.2 and Appendix F, Table 1). Token healing was previously illustrated but not quantitatively benchmarked.

E3.justification: v2 retains Llama 3.1 8B but replaces GPT2-large in the aggregate evaluation with Llama-3.2-1B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, and phi-4. It reports a 4000-byte prefix where v1 reported characters, adds K=2 and surprisal measurements, changes hardware, and introduces joint beam-size and pruning-threshold sweeps.

E4.justification: Beyond the existing beam-size error/speed analysis, Appendix G and Figure 2 systematically examine probability-threshold pruning across beam sizes and four models. They measure effects on error, speed, and surprisal, explicitly identifying empty-beam failures and infinite surprisal under excessive pruning.

E5.justification: Both versions report bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals for experimental averages. The additional results extend this reporting practice; no new repeated-run counts, seed information, or statistical testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 replaces and expands the benchmark results and adds surprisal, token-healing, and threshold-pruning outcomes. For Llama 3.1 8B at K=4, v1 reports 0.00021 JSD/character and 46.31 characters/second; v2 reports 0.00005 JSD/byte and 32.06 bytes/second under revised settings. Newly reported v2 surprisal is 0.53173 bits/byte, versus 0.66 for canonical tokenization and 2.116 for token healing.

T1.justification: The principal propositions and proofs are retained, with the correctness proofs moved to Appendices B and E and covering-size analysis moved to C. v2 formalizes prompt-boundary consistency through relative probabilities, introduces the token-healing covering and its size bound, and changes an equality to a lower bound in Proposition 4's proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add significant compression-rate improvement over canonical tokenization as a main empirical claim. v1 instead emphasized approximation accuracy and speed, including a specific Llama result. The central claims about character-level conversion and resolving the prompt boundary problem remain.

C2.justification: v2 explains surprisal gains through noncanonical probability mass and high-probability noncanonical tokenizations. It also explicitly identifies stochastic tokenizers, including UnigramLM and BPE-Dropout, as potentially requiring expensive large beams. These additions refine the retained explanation and limitation concerning concentration on relatively few tokenizations.

D1.justification: The code pointer changes from token-to-char-lm to genlm-bytes, and v2 documents the GenLM interface with a vLLM backend. Reported hardware changes from an A100 with 80GB to an L40S with 40GB. Appendices F and G provide implementation pseudocode for the new baseline and pruning variant; detailed trie implementation already existed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Loula et al. on constrained generation and Provilkov et al. on BPE-Dropout, while removing several background references, including Blum, Cotterell, and Goubault. Its positioning relative to token healing and prior tokenization-marginalization work remains largely unchanged. Gastaldi's publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses and edits the introduction, background, and algorithm exposition, removes redundant helper listings, and relocates the main correctness proofs to appendices. It separates the conclusion and limitations, adds an impact statement, and reorganizes the appendix structure around results, proofs, implementation, and additional experiments.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper with reformatted examples and pseudocode. The two-model error/speed display becomes a four-model figure with an additional surprisal row; numerical tables move to Appendix A. A token-healing table and a separate pruning-sensitivity figure are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation beyond v1's internal approximation/runtime comparison. Quantitative canonical-tokenization and token-healing comparisons establish practical benefits, while Appendix G examines pruning tradeoffs and failures. More specific tokenizer limitations improve qualification of the claims. Evaluation remains restricted to a short WikiText prefix, but the new comparisons resolve an important gap in the earlier paper's evidence.
